Every goroutine gets its own contiguous, heap-allocated stack.

blocks.title: Why copying is legal
blocks.text: Go has precise stack maps: the GC knows every pointer slot in every frame, so pointers into the old stack can be rewritten safely.

blocks.title: A goroutine leak is a memory leak
blocks.text: It holds its stack, its captured variables, and everything those reference. Ten thousand leaked handlers pin ten thousand request bodies.

caption.text: A goroutine costs 2 KB and about a microsecond — until one blocks forever, and then it costs you a stack, its captured variables, and eventually the pod. This handbook walks the whole runtime: G/M/P, what `schedule()` does 61 ticks at a time, how stacks grow by copying, the nine ways goroutines leak, and the pprof ladder for finding them. Save it for the next time RSS climbs while your heap stays flat.
